concepts.caption: A Bitcoin is always a Bitcoin. Ten years apart, the unit hasn't changed. The only real question is whether you held your own keys the whole time.
concepts.headline: 1 BTC = 1 BTC

concepts.novelty: Swaps the versus/price-comparison structure for the then_now format with zero dollar amounts anywhere, focused purely on unit permanence rather than purchasing power.
concepts.purpose: Reinforce Bitcoin's fixed-unit identity over time without any price framing.
concepts.rationale: Strong, often-repeated evergreen line, first use of the then_now catalog format on this board, cheap to build with zero price risk.
concepts.source_ref: "1 BTC = 1 BTC / The best stablecoin." tightened to "1 BTC = 1 BTC" for the headline, meaning kept exactly.
concepts.subject: one Bitcoin across ten years
concepts.visual_direction: Two-column layout, thin vertical divider down the middle. Left column labeled with an earlier year, right column labeled with a later year, each showing the numeral 1 BTC in matching weight. No dollar figures anywhere. Orange accent on the divider line only. Generous white space, logo bottom right.

concepts.novelty: Same format, entirely different message category: custody architecture and trust rather than market sentiment or conviction.
concepts.purpose: Reinforce trust in Relai's self-custodial model by stating plainly that it never holds user funds.
concepts.rationale: Strong trust-building evergreen line, rerun of the sole big_number format on the board but with a wholly different message.

concepts.subject: Relai holds zero user funds
concepts.visual_direction: Single giant numeral 0 centered on the frame, orange accent on the numeral itself, nothing else in the frame, no icons, no chart. Generous white space, logo bottom right.

concepts.caption: Self-custody sounds complicated until you break down the myths. Swipe through five things people get wrong about holding their own Bitcoin, from 'exchanges are safer' to 'I don't have enough to bother.'
flags: Naming specific past exchanges (Mt. Gox, FTX, Celsius) brushes against 'no comparisons to other brokers or exchanges', even though one such line is already pre-approved in the copy pool; confirm any new myth slides don't add fresh named comparisons
concepts.headline: SELF-CUSTODY MYTHS, DEBUNKED

concepts.novelty: Narrows scope specifically to self-custody myths rather than general Bitcoin misconceptions, Relai's clearest differentiator.
concepts.purpose: Address common hesitations about self-custody directly to build confidence in holding one's own keys.
concepts.rationale: Self-custody is Relai's core differentiator and recurs heavily across the approved pool, a dedicated myth carousel fills a gap next to the general misconceptions piece already on the board.
concepts.source_ref: Self-custody anxiety theme, evidenced by repeated approved lines: 'NOT YOUR KEYS NOT YOUR BITCOIN' (multiple variants), 'If you don't self-custody your Bitcoin, you don't actually own any Bitcoin', 'Self-custody history lesson: Mt. concepts.subject: common self-custody myths debunked
concepts.visual_direction: Consistent template per slide: the myth in quotes at the top, the rebuttal directly under it in one line, orange accent on the rebuttal text only, plain background, logo bottom right on every slide. No icons beyond simple quote marks.

concepts.caption: A padlock only works if you hold the key. Self-custody means you're the only one who can open yours. Hold your own keys, always.
concepts.headline: YOUR KEYS. YOUR BITCOIN.

concepts.subject: padlock with the key still in it

concepts.caption: No weekends off, no closing time. Bitcoin moves every day of the year, holidays included. Worth remembering next time a transfer is stuck 'processing' for three business days.
